5 Vector Semantics “Vector semantics” is the theory for representing meaning as vectors of numbers—the standard way to represent word meaning in NLP. Osgood et al., 1957 found that words varied along three important dimensions of affective meaning: • Words like happy or satisfied are high on valence (the opposite for unhappy or annoyed). • Excited is high on arousal, while calm is low on arousal. • Controlling is high on dominance, while influenced is low on dominance
Module Overview Vector Semantics (cont.) The idea that word meaning can be represented as a point in a high-dimensional space (beyond 3D) is the foundation of vector semantics.

9 Sampling for LLM Generation: Top-k Sampling • Top-k sampling is a simple generalisation of greedy decoding. • Instead of choosing the single most probable word to generate, 1. we first truncate the distribution to the top k most likely words, 2. renormalize to produce a legitimate probability distribution, and then 3. randomly sample from within these k words according to their renormalised probabilities.

11 Sampling for LLM Generation: Temperature Sampling • In temperature sampling, we don’t truncate the distribution, but reshape it instead. • In low-temperature sampling, we increase the probability of the most probable words and decrease the probability of rare words. • In moderately high-temperature sampling, we increase the probability of the most probable words and also the probability of rare words. • In very high-temperature sampling, we follow an equal distribution – i.e., random word selection.

15 CKY Parsing: Explanation • A 2D matrix is used to encode the structure of a parse tree. • The table is indexed by (i, j), with i=start & j=end of a span. • Each cell [𝑖, 𝑗] contains possible non-terminals that can generate that substring. • Since each non-terminal symbol has two children, a constituent can be split into two parts (sub-constituents): • the first constituent [𝑖, 𝑘] must lie to the left of entry [𝑖, 𝑗] somewhere along row 𝑖, and • the second entry [𝑘, 𝑗] must lie beneath it, along column 𝑗.

21 Dependency Parsing: Formalisation Since sentences can have multiple parses, CKY can be used to find all possible parse trees under a CFG. A dependency structure can be represented as a directed graph 𝐺 = (𝑉, 𝐴), consisting of vertices 𝑉 (words or punctuation), and a set of pairs of vertices 𝐴 called arcs. A dependency tree is a directed tree with these constraints: • There is a single designated root node that has no incoming arcs. • Except for the root node, each vertex has exactly one incoming arc. • There is a unique path from the root node to each vertex in 𝑉.

9 Sampling for LLM Generation: Top-k Sampling • Top-k sampling is a simple generalisation of greedy decoding. • Instead of choosing the single most probable word to generate, 1. we first truncate the distribution to the top k most likely words, 2. renormalize to produce a legitimate probability distribution, and then 3. randomly sample from within these k words according to their renormalised probabilities.

15 CKY Parsing: Explanation • A 2D matrix is used to encode the structure of a parse tree. • The table is indexed by (i, j), with i=start & j=end of a span. • Each cell [𝑖, 𝑗] contains possible non-terminals that can generate that substring. • Since each non-terminal symbol has two children, a constituent can be split into two parts (sub-constituents): • the first constituent [𝑖, 𝑘] must lie to the left of entry [𝑖, 𝑗] somewhere along row 𝑖, and • the second entry [𝑘, 𝑗] must lie beneath it, along column 𝑗.

21 Dependency Parsing: Formalisation Since sentences can have multiple parses, CKY can be used to find all possible parse trees under a CFG. A dependency structure can be represented as a directed graph 𝐺 = (𝑉, 𝐴), consisting of vertices 𝑉 (words or punctuation), and a set of pairs of vertices 𝐴 called arcs. A dependency tree is a directed tree with these constraints: • There is a single designated root node that has no incoming arcs. • Except for the root node, each vertex has exactly one incoming arc. • There is a unique path from the root node to each vertex in 𝑉.

9 Sampling for LLM Generation: Top-k Sampling • Top-k sampling is a simple generalisation of greedy decoding. • Instead of choosing the single most probable word to generate, 1. we first truncate the distribution to the top k most likely words, 2. renormalize to produce a legitimate probability distribution, and then 3. randomly sample from within these k words according to their renormalised probabilities.

11 Sampling for LLM Generation: Temperature Sampling • In temperature sampling, we don’t truncate the distribution, but reshape it instead. • In low-temperature sampling, we increase the probability of the most probable words and decrease the probability of rare words. • In moderately high-temperature sampling, we increase the probability of the most probable words and also the probability of rare words. • In very high-temperature sampling, we follow an equal distribution – i.e., random word selection.

21 In-Context Learning (ICL) The term in-context learning (ICL) was first proposed by Brown et al. (2020) as part of their GPT3 system. ICL means LLMs learning to do new tasks not explicitly trained for, better predict tokens at inference time, without any gradient-based updates to the model’s parameters. Benefits of ICL: • No need for finetuning • Flexible adaptation to different tasks • Improved performance over zero-shot prompting • Cost effective due to not retraining required Whilst few-shot prompting is a technique, ICL is the ability that makes few-shot & CoT prompting work.

15 CKY Parsing: Explanation • A 2D matrix is used to encode the structure of a parse tree. • The table is indexed by (i, j), with i=start & j=end of a span. • Each cell [𝑖, 𝑗] contains possible non-terminals that can generate that substring. • Since each non-terminal symbol has two children, a constituent can be split into two parts (sub-constituents): • the first constituent [𝑖, 𝑘] must lie to the left of entry [𝑖, 𝑗] somewhere along row 𝑖, and • the second entry [𝑘, 𝑗] must lie beneath it, along column 𝑗.

16 CKY Parsing: Algorithm Indexes: i = start position of a substring/span j = end position of a substring/span k = split point inside the substring table[i=start index,j=end index] Whilst the first "for all" fills the diagonal (cells table[j−1, j]), the other "for all" fills the non-diagonal cells.

21 Dependency Parsing: Formalisation Since sentences can have multiple parses, CKY can be used to find all possible parse trees under a CFG. A dependency structure can be represented as a directed graph 𝐺 = (𝑉, 𝐴), consisting of vertices 𝑉 (words or punctuation), and a set of pairs of vertices 𝐴 called arcs. A dependency tree is a directed tree with these constraints: • There is a single designated root node that has no incoming arcs. • Except for the root node, each vertex has exactly one incoming arc. • There is a unique path from the root node to each vertex in 𝑉.
